data.description:
Pinealon is a synthetic short-chain peptide bioregulator composed of three amino acids:

Glu–Asp–Arg (EDR)

It has been investigated primarily in neuroprotection, cognitive biology, cellular stress responses, neuronal gene regulation, and ageing-related research.

The supplied material describes Pinealon as originating from the Russian peptide-bioregulator research tradition and discusses experimental findings involving:

 	neuronal oxidative stress;
 	hypoxic injury;
 	apoptosis;
 	mitochondrial function;
 	gene-expression regulation;
 	cognitive performance;
 	circadian biology;
 	age-related cellular changes.

The Atlas Longevity Pinealon pen contains 20 mg in a 3 mL cartridge with 300 total units/clicks.

The evidence base for Pinealon is substantially more limited than that of established neurological medicines. Most of the supplied research is animal, in-vitro, or observational, with no established large-scale randomized human evidence or regulatory approval.



Clinical / Research Status
Pinealon remains an investigational peptide bioregulator.






Evidence Type
Status Based on Supplied Material




Human randomized clinical research

No






The supplied material discusses limited human observational findings alongside a larger body of preclinical research.

Claims involving cognitive enhancement, neuroprotection, longevity, sleep improvement, or anti-ageing should therefore remain experimental rather than established therapeutic claims.



Evidence Type
The source describes research involving:

 	aged-animal cognitive models;
 	cultured cortical neurons;
 	accelerated-ageing mouse models;
 	human fibroblast cultures;
 	neurotoxicity models;
 	limited elderly observational research;
 	ischemia-reperfusion models;
 	sleep-deprivation behavioural models.

These studies investigate different biological endpoints and should not all be interpreted as equivalent evidence of human clinical efficacy.



Mechanism of Action
Pinealon is investigated as a cell-penetrating tripeptide bioregulator.

The supplied material proposes that the Glu-Asp-Arg sequence may interact with cellular and nuclear regulatory systems involved in neuronal survival and stress responses.

Reported research mechanisms include:

 	modulation of gene expression;
 	regulation of neuronal survival pathways;
 	oxidative-stress reduction;
 	mitochondrial stabilisation;
 	apoptosis-related signalling;
 	possible epigenetic effects;
 	changes in neurotransmitter-related pathways.

Gene-Expression Regulation
One of Pinealon's defining research concepts is its proposed ability to influence transcription of genes involved in:

 	neuronal survival;
 	antioxidant defence;
 	apoptosis;
 	cellular adaptation.

The exact molecular interactions and their relevance in humans remain incompletely established.
Oxidative-Stress Research
Experimental work described in the source reports changes in:

 	reactive oxygen species;
 	antioxidant enzyme activity;
 	mitochondrial integrity;
 	stress-related cellular survival.

Neurotransmitter Research
The supplied material also discusses possible effects on serotonin metabolism and related neuronal signalling.

These mechanisms remain exploratory.



Potential Benefits / Research Areas
Cognitive Function Research
Pinealon has been studied in aged and stressed experimental models involving:

 	memory;
 	learning;
 	attention;
 	reaction time;
 	cognitive performance.

The source reports improvements in selected cognitive endpoints in animal models and limited observational research.

These findings do not establish Pinealon as a clinically proven cognitive enhancer.
Neuroprotection Research
A major Pinealon research area involves neuronal responses to:

 	oxidative stress;
 	hypoxia;
 	excitotoxicity;
 	neurotoxic exposure;
 	ischemic injury.

Experimental findings described by the source include reduced markers of neuronal damage and improved survival in selected models.
Oxidative-Stress Biology
The source discusses Pinealon in relation to endogenous antioxidant systems including:

 	superoxide dismutase;
 	catalase;
 	mitochondrial defence mechanisms.

These findings are mainly preclinical.
Apoptosis Research
Experimental models have examined whether Pinealon can influence programmed cell-death signalling under cellular stress.

Research described by the source includes changes in apoptosis-related pathways and neuronal survival markers.
Mitochondrial Research
Pinealon has also been investigated for possible effects on:

 	mitochondrial integrity;
 	oxidative damage;
 	energy-related cellular resilience.

This is particularly relevant to neurodegeneration and ageing models.
Cellular Ageing Research
The supplied material discusses Pinealon as a peptide bioregulator involved in experimental ageing research.

Reported areas include:

 	cellular longevity;
 	telomerase-related activity;
 	telomere biology;
 	age-related gene-expression changes.

These findings do not establish extension of human lifespan or reversal of human ageing.
Circadian Rhythm Research
Pinealon has also been investigated in relation to:

 	pineal biology;
 	melatonin-associated rhythms;
 	sleep-wake regulation;
 	circadian signalling.

The evidence described remains limited and primarily experimental.
Stress-Response Research
Animal models have investigated Pinealon during physical or psychological stress.

The source proposes effects involving:

 	HPA-axis signalling;
 	cellular adaptation;
 	cognitive resilience.

These are research observations rather than established therapeutic effects.
Retinal and Visual Research
The supplied material also discusses experimental retinal models involving:

 	photoreceptor preservation;
 	ischemic stress;
 	electrophysiological responses;
 	age-related retinal changes.

Human ophthalmological efficacy is not established.

Most of these findings are preclinical, and the limited observational evidence should not be treated as proof of clinical effectiveness.



Potential Stack / Combination Research

The proposed rationale involves combining pathways related to:

The supplied information does not establish validated human safety, compatibility, efficacy, or dosing for these combinations.

They should therefore be treated strictly as experimental research concepts.

data.description:
Somatropin (recombinant human growth hormone / rhGH) is a 191-amino-acid peptide hormone designed to match endogenous human growth hormone produced by the pituitary gland.

Growth hormone plays a central role in growth, metabolism, tissue turnover, protein synthesis, lipid mobilisation, bone biology, and IGF-1 signalling. Somatropin has therefore been extensively investigated in clinical and experimental research involving growth hormone deficiency, body composition, connective tissue, skeletal physiology, and metabolic regulation.

Somatropin acts both directly through the growth hormone receptor (GHR) and indirectly by stimulating production of insulin-like growth factor-1 (IGF-1).

Atlas Longevity Somatropin pens are available in:

 	10 IU HGH Pen
 	36 IU HGH Pen

Both use the Atlas standard:

3 mL cartridge volume

300 total pen units / clicks

1 click = 0.01 mL

The 10 IU variant replaces the previously referenced 24 IU pen. The 36 IU variant remains available.



Clinical / Research Status
Somatropin has a substantially stronger clinical evidence base than most experimental peptides.






Evidence Type
Status




Human randomized clinical research
Yes


Human observational research
Yes


Animal research
Yes


In-vitro research
Yes


Regulatory therapeutic use
Yes, for specific approved indications






The supplied material describes Somatropin as an FDA-approved growth hormone medication for specific clinical conditions while emphasizing that uses outside approved indications remain investigational.

Approval of specific prescription Somatropin products should not automatically be interpreted as approval of the Atlas Longevity Somatropin pen or of anti-ageing, bodybuilding, performance-enhancement, or cosmetic uses.



Mechanism of Action
Somatropin binds to growth hormone receptors (GHRs) located throughout multiple tissues.

Growth hormone receptor activation initiates intracellular signalling involving:

 	JAK2
 	STAT5
 	MAPK / ERK
 	PI3K / Akt
 	downstream mTOR-related signalling

These pathways influence gene transcription involved in:

 	cellular growth;
 	protein metabolism;
 	tissue differentiation;
 	repair processes;
 	lipid metabolism.

IGF-1 Signalling
A major downstream effect of growth hormone is stimulation of IGF-1 production, particularly in the liver.

IGF-1 contributes to many of the anabolic and growth-related effects associated with the GH axis, including signalling within:

 	skeletal muscle;
 	bone;
 	connective tissue;
 	cartilage;
 	other growth-responsive tissues.

Lipid Metabolism
Growth hormone also influences adipose-tissue metabolism and lipolytic pathways.

These metabolic actions are separate from its growth-promoting effects and are an important area of GH research.



Potential Benefits / Research Areas
Growth Hormone and IGF-1 Research
Somatropin is one of the principal compounds used to study direct growth hormone receptor activation.

Unlike GHRH analogues or secretagogues, Somatropin provides the growth hormone molecule itself rather than stimulating the pituitary to increase endogenous release.

This makes it useful for research comparing:

 	direct GH exposure;
 	GHRH stimulation;
 	ghrelin-receptor secretagogues;
 	downstream IGF-1 responses.

Protein Synthesis and Lean-Tissue Research
Growth hormone and IGF-1 are involved in protein metabolism.

Research has examined effects involving:

 	amino-acid utilisation;
 	nitrogen retention;
 	protein turnover;
 	lean body mass;
 	skeletal-muscle signalling.

Changes in lean mass do not necessarily translate directly into proportional increases in functional strength or athletic performance.
Adipose-Tissue and Lipolysis Research
Somatropin has also been studied for its ability to influence:

 	fat mobilisation;
 	adipocyte metabolism;
 	visceral adipose tissue;
 	lipid oxidation.

This makes GH important in metabolic and body-composition research.

It should not be presented as an approved general fat-loss treatment.
Bone and Skeletal Research
Growth hormone and IGF-1 influence:

 	osteoblast activity;
 	bone turnover;
 	skeletal growth;
 	collagen synthesis;
 	mineralisation.

Somatropin is therefore widely studied in growth and skeletal biology.
Connective-Tissue and Collagen Research
Experimental studies investigate GH/IGF-1 signalling in relation to:

 	fibroblast activity;
 	collagen production;
 	extracellular matrix turnover;
 	tissue remodelling.

These mechanisms provide a basis for regenerative research but do not establish guaranteed healing effects.
Metabolic Research
Growth hormone has complex effects on glucose and lipid metabolism.

Experimental endpoints include:

 	insulin sensitivity;
 	glucose utilisation;
 	hepatic metabolism;
 	lipid profiles;
 	substrate distribution.

Importantly, increased GH exposure can also reduce insulin sensitivity, so its metabolic effects should not be characterized as universally beneficial.
Neurological and Neuroendocrine Research
GH and IGF-1 signalling also interact with the nervous system.

Research areas include:

 	neuroendocrine regulation;
 	cognition;
 	sleep;
 	brain GH signalling;
 	neuronal IGF-1 pathways.

Evidence for direct cognitive enhancement remains less established than the endocrine and growth-related effects of Somatropin.
Skin and Extracellular-Matrix Research
Somatropin-related studies have also examined:

 	dermal collagen;
 	skin thickness;
 	tissue hydration;
 	extracellular-matrix biology.

These findings should remain framed as research rather than proven cosmetic anti-ageing outcomes.



Research Data






Study / Model
Reported Finding




GH-deficient adult clinical studies
Increased lean body mass and reduced fat mass reported during GH replacement


Older-adult research
Changes in skin thickness and collagen-related measurements


Fracture animal models
Increased callus formation and osteoblast-related activity


Wound-healing research
Increased fibroblast activity and collagen synthesis in experimental systems


Human metabolic studies
Changes in lipid metabolism and glucose-related endpoints


Exercise and recovery studies
Changes in body composition and recovery-related markers


In-vitro cell research
Increased STAT5 signalling and IGF-1 gene expression


Long-term experimental models
Sustained effects on protein turnover and metabolic signalling






Clinical outcomes depend strongly on the population studied, underlying GH status, exposure, duration, and formulation.



Somatropin vs GH Secretagogues
Somatropin should be distinguished from compounds such as:

 	CJC-1295;
 	Tesamorelin;
 	Ipamorelin;
 	GHRP-6.

Somatropin
Provides growth hormone directly.
GHRH Analogues
Compounds such as CJC-1295 and Tesamorelin stimulate the pituitary through the GHRH receptor.
Ghrelin-Receptor Secretagogues
Compounds such as Ipamorelin stimulate GH release through the GHS-R1a / ghrelin receptor pathway.

These approaches affect the GH axis differently and should not be treated as interchangeable.



Potential Stack / Combination Research
The supplied material discusses experimental combinations involving Somatropin with:

 	IGF-1 LR3;
 	BPC-157;
 	TB-500;
 	Epitalon;
 	SS-31;
 	NAD+;
 	CJC-1295;
 	Ipamorelin.

These combinations involve overlapping pathways related to growth signalling, regeneration, metabolism, or mitochondrial research.

Combining direct HGH with GH-releasing compounds can also increase overall GH/IGF-1 pathway exposure.

The supplied information does not establish validated safety, efficacy, compatibility, or dosing for these combinations.

They should therefore be treated as experimental research concepts rather than recommended stacks.

data.description:
CJC-1295 with DAC is a synthetic long-acting analogue of growth hormone-releasing hormone (GHRH) designed to produce sustained stimulation of the growth hormone (GH) and insulin-like growth factor-1 (IGF-1) axis.

The peptide contains a Drug Affinity Complex (DAC) modification that enables prolonged association with circulating albumin. This substantially extends its biological persistence compared with native GHRH and shorter-acting GHRH analogues.

Research has examined CJC-1295 with DAC in relation to:

 	endogenous growth hormone secretion;
 	circulating IGF-1;
 	pituitary GHRH receptor signalling;
 	GH pulse amplitude;
 	metabolic regulation;
 	body-composition biology;
 	tissue-repair signalling;
 	prolonged somatotropic-axis activation.

The Atlas Longevity CJC-1295 with DAC pen contains 5 mg in a 3 mL cartridge with 300 total units/clicks.

CJC-1295 with DAC remains an investigational research peptide. The supplied material describes early human pharmacokinetic research alongside animal and in-vitro evidence, but it is not presented as an approved medicine.



Clinical / Research Status
The supplied material describes CJC-1295 with DAC as having undergone limited early-phase human investigation, particularly in pharmacokinetic and GH/IGF-1 research.






Evidence Type
Status Based on Supplied Material




Human randomized clinical research
Not established by supplied status section


Human observational / early-phase research
Yes

Yes

No






The source's evidence table marks human RCT evidence as absent while some later references are labelled as human RCTs. For Atlas content, the more cautious description is therefore limited human pharmacokinetic and endocrine research rather than a broad established clinical evidence base.



Evidence Type
The supplied material describes research involving:

 	healthy adult human pharmacokinetic studies;
 	repeated human exposure studies;
 	pituitary-cell research;
 	GHRH receptor assays;
 	aged-animal models;
 	growth-hormone-deficient animal models.

The strongest source-supported findings concern prolonged GH and IGF-1 elevation following CJC-1295 with DAC exposure.

Claims involving muscle gain, fat loss, sleep, skin rejuvenation, bone density, or anti-ageing should remain secondary and research-oriented.



Mechanism of Action
CJC-1295 with DAC acts as a GHRH receptor agonist.

It binds to GHRH receptors on anterior pituitary somatotroph cells, stimulating endogenous growth hormone secretion.

The resulting increase in GH can subsequently increase production of:

IGF-1

primarily through hepatic GH signalling.
GHRH Receptor Activation
Activation of the GHRH receptor stimulates intracellular signalling associated with:

 	adenylate cyclase;
 	cAMP;
 	protein kinase A;
 	GH synthesis;
 	GH secretion.

Drug Affinity Complex (DAC)
The defining feature of CJC-1295 with DAC is its albumin-binding DAC modification.

The source describes this as allowing prolonged association with serum albumin, substantially slowing peptide clearance.

This is the basis for the source-reported half-life of approximately:

6–8 days

compared with the much shorter persistence of native GHRH.
Sustained GH / IGF-1 Signalling
Because the compound remains biologically available for longer, experimental exposure can produce more prolonged changes in:

 	mean GH concentration;
 	GH pulse amplitude;
 	IGF-1 levels.

The supplied material specifically describes sustained increases rather than complete replacement of physiological GH pulsatility.



CJC-1295 with DAC vs CJC-1295 No-DAC
The two compounds should not be treated as interchangeable.
CJC-1295 with DAC
Designed for long-duration systemic exposure through albumin binding.

Source-reported half-life:

approximately 6–8 days
CJC-1295 No-DAC
A much shorter-acting GHRH analogue without the albumin-binding DAC modification.

Its pharmacokinetic behaviour and research design are therefore substantially different.

Any click calculations, timing concepts, or research interpretation should be kept specific to the exact CJC-1295 variant being discussed.



Potential Benefits / Research Areas
Sustained Growth Hormone Research
The main research characteristic of CJC-1295 with DAC is its ability to produce prolonged stimulation of endogenous GH secretion.

Human research described by the source reports elevated mean GH concentrations for several days following exposure.

This makes CJC-1295 with DAC useful in models examining chronic rather than brief GHRH receptor stimulation.
IGF-1 Research
Increased GH signalling can raise circulating IGF-1.

The source reports prolonged IGF-1 elevations following CJC-1295 with DAC administration, extending beyond the initial GH response.

This is one of the most clearly described downstream endpoints in the supplied material.
GH Pulsatility Research
The source states that CJC-1295 with DAC can increase GH pulse amplitude while preserving endogenous pulsatile characteristics.

This makes the compound relevant to research into:

 	somatotropic-axis physiology;
 	GH pulse architecture;
 	long-duration GHRH stimulation.

Body-Composition Research
Because the GH/IGF-1 axis influences protein and lipid metabolism, CJC-1295 with DAC has been studied in experimental models involving:

 	lean tissue;
 	adipose tissue;
 	protein metabolism;
 	body composition.

Most claims involving significant muscle gain or fat loss remain more preclinical than established human outcomes.
Lipolysis Research
Growth hormone participates in adipose-tissue metabolism and lipolytic signalling.

The supplied source discusses experimental reductions in visceral and subcutaneous fat in selected models.

These findings should not be translated into guaranteed human fat-loss outcomes.
Tissue-Repair Research
The GH–IGF-1 axis participates in:

 	fibroblast signalling;
 	collagen synthesis;
 	satellite-cell biology;
 	connective-tissue turnover.

CJC-1295 with DAC is therefore discussed in experimental tissue-repair and recovery research.

This does not establish the compound as an approved treatment for injury or musculoskeletal repair.
Sleep and GH-Release Research
Growth hormone secretion is physiologically associated with sleep, particularly slow-wave sleep.

The supplied source discusses CJC-1295 with DAC in relation to sleep architecture and nocturnal GH signalling.

However, evidence for direct sleep improvement is weaker than the pharmacokinetic evidence for GH and IGF-1 elevation.

GH and IGF-1 influence bone remodelling.

Experimental research described by the source discusses:

 	osteoblast activity;
 	collagen type I;
 	mineralisation;
 	skeletal remodelling.

These findings remain research-oriented and should not be presented as proof of improved human bone density.

The source also discusses experimental effects on dermal collagen and extracellular-matrix biology.

This provides a mechanistic basis for skin-related research but does not establish anti-ageing or cosmetic rejuvenation outcomes.
Metabolic Research
Sustained GH elevation can influence:

 	glucose metabolism;
 	insulin sensitivity;
 	lipid metabolism;
 	substrate utilisation.

These effects can be complex and may include reduced insulin sensitivity rather than uniformly beneficial metabolic changes.

Product Description
Tesamorelin is a synthetic analogue of growth hormone-releasing hormone (GHRH) studied for its ability to stimulate endogenous growth hormone secretion through the pituitary gland.

Rather than supplying growth hormone directly, Tesamorelin activates the body's GHRH receptor pathway, increasing pulsatile growth hormone signalling and subsequently influencing circulating IGF-1. Clinical research has focused particularly on visceral adipose tissue, metabolic function, lipid biology, liver-related outcomes, and the broader GH–IGF-1 axis. Pasted markdown

Atlas Longevity Tesamorelin pens use the standard 3 mL / 300-click cartridge system and are available in:

 	10 mg Tesamorelin
 	20 mg Tesamorelin

Tesamorelin has undergone substantial human clinical investigation and has regulatory approval for a specific HIV-associated lipodystrophy indication. That regulatory history applies to authorized Tesamorelin products and indications and should not automatically be interpreted as approval of the Atlas Longevity pen or of unrelated anti-ageing, body-composition, performance, or longevity uses. Clinical / Research Status
Tesamorelin has a considerably stronger clinical evidence base than many experimental peptides.

Evidence Type

 	multicentre randomized human studies;
 	HIV-associated visceral-fat research;
 	metabolic and lipid studies;
 	liver-fat research;
 	pituitary-receptor assays;
 	muscle and body-composition research;
 	neurocognitive pilot research;
 	observational studies. Pasted markdown

The strongest human evidence relates to GH/IGF-1 signalling and visceral adipose tissue in defined clinical populations, while claims involving anti-ageing, performance enhancement, skin rejuvenation, or lifespan extension are substantially less established.



Mechanism of Action
Tesamorelin binds to growth hormone-releasing hormone receptors (GHRHR) located on pituitary somatotroph cells.

According to the supplied material, receptor activation stimulates the:

Gαs → adenylate cyclase → cAMP → PKA pathway

which promotes growth hormone synthesis and pulsatile secretion.

The resulting increase in circulating GH can then stimulate hepatic production of IGF-1, which participates in downstream pathways involving:

 	PI3K-Akt;
 	mTOR;
 	JAK-STAT;
 	protein metabolism;
 	lipolysis;
 	tissue signalling. Pasted markdown

Tesamorelin acts upstream at the pituitary gland rather than supplying exogenous growth hormone directly.

Tesamorelin is primarily studied as a GHRH receptor agonist capable of increasing endogenous GH release.

What is Tesamorelin?
Tesamorelin is a synthetic analogue of growth hormone-releasing hormone (GHRH).

data.description:
Cagrilintide is a synthetic long-acting analogue of amylin, a hormone normally co-secreted with insulin by pancreatic beta cells.

Amylin participates in the regulation of satiety, meal size, gastric emptying, postprandial glucose handling, and energy intake. Cagrilintide has been structurally modified to provide substantially longer biological activity than native amylin, allowing sustained investigation of amylin-receptor signalling.

Human clinical research has examined Cagrilintide in relation to:

 	appetite regulation;
 	reduced energy intake;
 	body-weight change;
 	obesity research;
 	gastric-emptying physiology;
 	metabolic regulation;
 	combination incretin-based research.

The Atlas Longevity Cagrilintide pen contains 5 mg in a 3 mL cartridge with 300 total units/clicks.

Cagrilintide remains an investigational metabolic compound within the material supplied. Human clinical evidence exists, but the source does not establish general regulatory approval for the Atlas Longevity formulation or for routine weight-management treatment.



Clinical / Research Status
Cagrilintide has progressed into substantial human clinical investigation, particularly in overweight, obesity, and metabolic research.






Evidence Type
Status Based on Supplied Material

Yes

Yes

Yes


In-vitro research
Yes


General regulatory approval
Not established by supplied material






The source describes multiple human studies examining Cagrilintide alone and in combination with GLP-1-related compounds.

Human research provides more direct evidence than exists for many experimental peptides, but findings remain formulation-, population-, and protocol-specific.



Evidence Type
The supplied material describes research involving:

 	Phase 1b studies in adults with overweight or obesity;
 	human satiety studies;
 	metabolic profiling;
 	combination research with GLP-1 SMA;
 	diet-induced obesity animal models;
 	amylin-receptor binding assays.

The strongest source-supported areas are appetite regulation, satiety, food-intake reduction, and body-weight research.

Claims involving broader metabolic optimisation should remain secondary to those established research domains.



Mechanism of Action
Cagrilintide acts primarily as a long-acting amylin receptor agonist.

Amylin receptors are not single standalone receptors. They are formed from combinations of:

 	the calcitonin receptor;
 	receptor activity-modifying proteins (RAMPs).

These receptor complexes are expressed in areas of the nervous system involved in appetite and satiety regulation.
Central Satiety Signalling
Cagrilintide activates amylin-sensitive signalling in brain regions including the:

 	area postrema;
 	brainstem;
 	hypothalamic appetite-control networks.

These regions integrate circulating nutrient-related signals and contribute to:

 	meal termination;
 	fullness;
 	hunger regulation;
 	energy intake.

Gastric Emptying
Amylin signalling also influences gastrointestinal motility.

Slower gastric emptying can alter:

 	nutrient delivery;
 	post-meal glucose appearance;
 	duration of fullness;
 	postprandial satiety.

Long-Acting Design
Native amylin is cleared relatively quickly.

Cagrilintide has been engineered for prolonged activity, allowing substantially more sustained receptor engagement and making it useful in longer-duration metabolic research.



Potential Benefits / Research Areas
Satiety and Appetite Research
Cagrilintide is primarily investigated for its influence on physiological satiety pathways rather than stimulant-style appetite suppression.

Activation of amylin receptors influences central circuits involved in:

 	hunger;
 	fullness;
 	meal size;
 	food-seeking behaviour.

This is one of the principal mechanistic foundations of Cagrilintide research.
Energy-Intake Research
Human studies have examined whether sustained amylin signalling can reduce overall energy intake.

The mechanism appears to act upstream by altering appetite and meal-related signalling rather than directly increasing metabolic rate.
Body-Weight Research
Clinical research has examined Cagrilintide in adults with overweight or obesity.

The supplied source reports body-weight reductions in selected controlled studies, including substantial changes over multi-month research periods.

These study-specific findings should not be interpreted as guaranteed results for every population or formulation.
Gastric-Emptying Research
Cagrilintide is also relevant to research involving:

 	delayed gastric emptying;
 	prolonged postprandial fullness;
 	nutrient-delivery kinetics;
 	post-meal metabolic responses.

This peripheral mechanism complements its central satiety activity.
Postprandial Metabolic Research
Amylin is naturally co-secreted with insulin.

Research therefore examines how Cagrilintide-related amylin signalling interacts with:

 	nutrient processing;
 	postprandial glucose regulation;
 	pancreatic signalling;
 	energy homeostasis.

Amylin Receptor Biology
Cagrilintide provides a model for investigating signalling through calcitonin receptor/RAMP complexes.

This includes research into:

 	receptor specificity;
 	ligand binding;
 	sustained receptor activation;
 	neural appetite circuitry.

Combination Incretin Research
A major area of interest involves combining amylin signalling with incretin pathways.

GLP-1 receptor agonism and amylin receptor agonism influence energy intake through overlapping but distinct mechanisms.

The supplied source specifically discusses combination research with GLP-1 SMA, including the investigational CagriSema concept.

Changes in glycaemic and lipid-related markers alongside weight reduction

The other combinations should be treated more cautiously.

It also influences gastric emptying, which can prolong fullness and alter post-meal nutrient delivery.
Where are amylin receptors located?
Important sites include the area postrema and hypothalamic appetite-regulation pathways.

These regions help integrate circulating nutrient signals with central hunger and satiety responses.
What are RAMPs?
RAMPs are receptor activity-modifying proteins.

Amylin receptors are formed when calcitonin receptors associate with particular RAMP proteins.

These combinations alter receptor pharmacology and ligand specificity.
Is Cagrilintide a GLP-1 receptor agonist?
No.

Cagrilintide is primarily an amylin analogue, not a GLP-1 receptor agonist.

However, amylin and GLP-1 pathways can influence overlapping aspects of appetite and energy regulation.
Is Cagrilintide the same as GLP-1 SMA?
No.

Cagrilintide primarily targets amylin receptor systems, while GLP-1 SMA acts through the GLP-1 receptor.

The two have been investigated together because they affect energy balance through distinct but complementary pathways.
What is CagriSema?
The supplied material uses CagriSema to describe research involving Cagrilintide together with GLP-1 SMA.

Combination-study findings should not automatically be applied to Cagrilintide alone.
What is Cagrilintide researched for?

 	satiety;

Has Cagrilintide been studied in humans?
Yes.

The supplied material describes multiple controlled human trials involving overweight, obesity, metabolic regulation, and combination therapy.
Does Cagrilintide reduce body weight?
Human clinical research described in the source reports body-weight reductions in selected study populations.

Those results are specific to particular trial designs, doses, durations, and populations and should not be treated as guaranteed outcomes.
Does Cagrilintide slow gastric emptying?
Amylin receptor activation can slow gastric emptying.

The supplied source discusses delayed gastric emptying and prolonged postprandial fullness as part of Cagrilintide's research profile.
Does Cagrilintide suppress appetite?
Appetite and satiety regulation are major research endpoints for Cagrilintide.

Its mechanism involves physiological satiety pathways rather than stimulant-mediated appetite suppression.

How many clicks are in the pen?

with:

1 click = 0.01 mL

How many clicks equal 0.25 mg?

How many clicks equal 0.3 mg?

data.name: NAD+ Pen
data.description:
NAD+ 500 mg / 1000 mg Pen
Product Description
NAD+ (Nicotinamide Adenine Dinucleotide) is an endogenous coenzyme central to cellular energy metabolism, redox reactions, mitochondrial respiration, and intracellular signalling.

NAD exists primarily in two interconvertible forms:

 	NAD+ — the oxidized form
 	NADH — the reduced form

Together, these molecules participate in electron-transfer reactions that help cells convert nutrients into usable energy through metabolic pathways including glycolysis, the tricarboxylic acid cycle, and oxidative phosphorylation.

NAD+ also serves as a substrate for enzymes including sirtuins and PARPs, connecting NAD biology with DNA repair, cellular stress responses, gene regulation, inflammation research, and mitochondrial function. Pasted text

Atlas Longevity NAD+ pens use the standard 3 mL / 300-click cartridge system and are available in:

 	500 mg NAD+
 	1000 mg NAD+

NAD+ is naturally present in the body, but injectable NAD+ preparations remain investigational and should not be presented as approved treatments for ageing, fatigue, cognitive decline, metabolic disease, or other medical conditions. Pasted text



Clinical / Research Status
NAD biology has been studied extensively across human, animal, and cellular research.

However, there is an important distinction between research into:

 	endogenous NAD metabolism;
 	NAD+ itself;
 	NAD precursors such as NMN or NR;
 	intravenous NAD+;
 	other injectable NAD+ formulations.

The supplied material states that injectable and IV NAD+ preparations are used experimentally but are not approved for therapeutic purposes. Pasted text






Evidence Type
Status Based on Supplied Material




Human clinical research
Yes


Human observational research
Yes


Animal research
Yes


In-vitro research
Yes


Regulatory approval for Atlas NAD+ pen
Not established






Evidence involving NMN or nicotinamide riboside should not automatically be presented as direct evidence for an NAD+ injection pen.



Evidence Type
The supplied material includes research involving:

 	intravenous NAD+ administration;
 	human observational metabolic research;
 	animal ageing models;
 	cellular ageing models;
 	neuronal cell cultures;
 	metabolic-disease models;
 	exercise-related research;
 	brain-ischaemia experimental models. Pasted text

The clinical relevance of these studies varies substantially depending on formulation, route of administration, species, and research endpoint.



Mechanism of Action
NAD+ is a central participant in cellular oxidation-reduction reactions.

During energy metabolism, NAD+ accepts electrons and becomes NADH. NADH can then donate electrons within mitochondrial pathways involved in ATP generation.

The supplied material describes NAD+ involvement in:

 	glycolysis;
 	the TCA / Krebs cycle;
 	oxidative phosphorylation;
 	electron transport;
 	ATP generation;
 	PARP-mediated DNA repair;
 	sirtuin activity;
 	mitochondrial biogenesis;
 	stress-response signalling;
 	AMPK-associated pathways. Pasted text

Sirtuin Signalling
Sirtuins are NAD-dependent enzymes involved in metabolic regulation, gene expression, stress responses, and mitochondrial biology.

Because sirtuin activity requires NAD+, changes in cellular NAD availability may alter several downstream signalling systems.
PARP and DNA Repair
PARP enzymes also consume NAD+ during responses to DNA damage.

This relationship has generated substantial interest in NAD metabolism within research involving cellular ageing and genomic stability.

These mechanisms establish NAD+ as an essential biological molecule but do not by themselves prove that additional injectable NAD+ produces anti-ageing or disease-treatment effects.



Potential Benefits / Research Areas
Cellular Energy and ATP Research
NAD+ is essential for numerous redox reactions involved in cellular energy metabolism.

Research examines how NAD+/NADH balance affects:

 	mitochondrial respiration;
 	nutrient metabolism;
 	ATP generation;
 	cellular energy availability. Pasted text

Frequently Asked Questions
What is NAD+?
NAD+ stands for Nicotinamide Adenine Dinucleotide.

It is an endogenous coenzyme required for numerous cellular redox reactions and plays a central role in energy metabolism and mitochondrial function. Pasted text
Is NAD+ a peptide?
No.

NAD+ is a nucleotide coenzyme, not a peptide.

Therefore, it does not have an amino-acid sequence.
What is the difference between NAD+ and NADH?
NAD+ is the oxidized form, while NADH is the reduced form.

The two continuously cycle between these states during cellular redox reactions and energy metabolism. Pasted text
How does NAD+ work?
NAD+ accepts and transfers electrons during metabolic reactions.

It also serves as a required substrate for several enzyme families, including sirtuins and PARPs, linking NAD biology to metabolism, mitochondrial function, DNA repair, and stress-response signalling. Pasted text

Does NAD+ activate sirtuins?

This relationship is one of the major reasons NAD metabolism is studied in ageing and metabolic biology. Pasted text
Does NAD+ repair DNA?
NAD+ is consumed by PARP enzymes involved in DNA-damage responses.

It therefore plays an important biochemical role in DNA-repair pathways, but describing NAD+ itself as directly “repairing DNA” would oversimplify the mechanism.

PT-141 10 mg Pen
Product Description
PT-141 (Bremelanotide) is a synthetic melanocortin receptor agonist derived from alpha-melanocyte-stimulating hormone research and studied primarily for its effects on central sexual-arousal pathways, melanocortin signalling, motivation, and hypothalamic neurobiology.

Unlike compounds that act mainly through peripheral vasodilation, PT-141 works primarily through the central nervous system, particularly melanocortin receptors associated with neural pathways involved in sexual desire and arousal.

Clinical and preclinical research described in the supplied material links PT-141 with activation of MC4R and MC3R, downstream dopaminergic signalling, and limbic-system pathways involved in sexual motivation. Pasted text

The Atlas Longevity PT-141 pen contains 10 mg in a 3 mL cartridge with 300 total units/clicks.

Bremelanotide has been clinically investigated and approved in certain jurisdictions for specific sexual-desire indications. However, approval applies to particular authorized formulations, populations, and indications and should not be interpreted as approval of the Atlas Longevity PT-141 pen.



Clinical / Research Status
PT-141 has a meaningful human evidence base compared with many investigational peptides.

That regulatory history should not be generalized to all PT-141 formulations or unapproved uses.



Evidence Type
The supplied material includes research involving:

 	Phase 3 studies in women with HSDD;
 	clinical research in men with erectile dysfunction;
 	rodent hypothalamic models;
 	subcutaneous pharmacokinetic studies;
 	non-human primate behavioural models;
 	healthy-volunteer research;
 	in-vitro melanocortin receptor-binding studies. Pasted text

This gives PT-141 a combination of human, animal, pharmacological, and receptor-level evidence.



Mechanism of Action
PT-141 acts primarily through central melanocortin receptors, especially MC4R and MC3R.

Activation of these receptors in hypothalamic and limbic pathways can influence:

 	sexual motivation;
 	arousal signalling;
 	dopaminergic activity;
 	reward-related neural circuits;
 	behavioural response.

The supplied material distinguishes PT-141 from PDE-5 inhibitors because its mechanism does not primarily depend on nitric-oxide-mediated peripheral vasodilation. Pasted text

Instead, PT-141 acts further upstream through central neural pathways associated with desire and arousal.
MC4R and MC3R Signalling
The supplied material describes PT-141 binding to melanocortin receptors and influencing intracellular cAMP-related signalling.

Research also discusses downstream effects involving dopaminergic pathways and POMC-related hypothalamic systems. Pasted text

Central Sexual-Arousal Research
PT-141 is primarily studied for its effects on central neural circuits involved in sexual desire and motivation.

Clinical research described by the source has examined desire-related endpoints and satisfying sexual-event measures in controlled populations. Pasted text

This differs from compounds whose main action is peripheral vascular response.
MC4R and MC3R Research
PT-141 interacts primarily with MC4R and MC3R, two receptor subtypes involved in central melanocortin signalling.

Research focuses on how activation of these receptors influences:

 	cAMP signalling;
 	dopamine-related pathways;
 	motivational behaviour;
 	hypothalamic and limbic activity. Pasted text

Dopaminergic Reward-Signalling Research
The source describes PT-141 in relation to mesolimbic dopamine pathways involved in reward anticipation and sexual motivation.

This makes it relevant to experimental research involving the relationship between melanocortin signalling and central motivational circuits. Pasted text
Research Distinct from PDE-5 Inhibitors
PT-141's mechanism is different from sildenafil-type compounds.

According to the supplied material, PT-141 does not primarily depend on nitric oxide or peripheral smooth-muscle vasodilation.

Instead, it acts through central melanocortin pathways. Pasted text

This mechanistic distinction is important when describing the compound accurately.

The supplied material references randomized human studies involving women with hypoactive sexual desire research diagnoses.

These trials examined changes in sexual-desire scores and satisfying sexual events. Pasted text

These findings apply to defined clinical populations and should not be generalized beyond the populations and formulations studied.

This does not make PT-141 interchangeable with conventional vascular erectile-function treatments.

Product Description
Epithalon, also known as Epitalon, is a synthetic tetrapeptide composed of four amino acids: alanine, glutamic acid, aspartic acid, and glycine (AEDG).

It originates from research involving epithalamin, a pineal-derived preparation investigated in ageing biology. Epithalon subsequently became a subject of experimental research focused on telomerase activity, telomere biology, cellular senescence, circadian signalling, oxidative stress, and longevity-related cellular pathways. Pasted text

One of its best-known research areas involves whether Epithalon can influence telomerase, an enzyme involved in maintaining telomeric DNA at chromosome ends during cellular replication.

The Atlas Longevity Epithalon pen contains 20 mg in a 3 mL pre-mixed cartridge with 300 total units/clicks.

Epithalon remains an investigational research peptide and should not be presented as an approved anti-ageing, longevity, sleep, or medical treatment.



Clinical / Research Status
Epithalon has primarily been investigated in preclinical, laboratory, and regional ageing research, with limited exploratory human evidence.

Evidence strength varies significantly between these areas.



Mechanism of Action
Epithalon is primarily researched for its potential influence on telomerase activity and telomere biology.

Telomeres are repetitive DNA structures located at chromosome ends. They protect chromosomes during cellular replication but generally become progressively shorter as cells divide.

Telomerase is an enzyme capable of extending telomeric DNA.

Laboratory studies referenced in the supplied material have investigated whether Epithalon can increase telomerase activity and influence telomere maintenance in dividing human cells. Pasted text

Beyond telomere biology, Epithalon has also been explored in research involving:

 	cellular senescence;
 	chromosomal stability;
 	pineal signalling;
 	melatonin rhythms;
 	oxidative-stress responses;
 	circadian regulation.

The precise biological effects and their relevance to human ageing remain under investigation.



Potential Benefits / Research Areas
Telomerase Activation Research
Epithalon is particularly associated with experimental research into telomerase activation.

In laboratory cell models, researchers have investigated whether Epithalon can influence telomerase activity and consequently affect telomere length in dividing cells. Pasted text

These results are scientifically interesting, but increased telomerase activity in cultured cells does not demonstrate that Epithalon extends human lifespan.
Telomere Maintenance
Telomeres progressively shorten during repeated cell division.

Because critically shortened telomeres can contribute to replicative senescence, researchers have investigated whether maintaining telomeric DNA could influence cellular ageing processes.

Epithalon's proposed influence on this pathway places it within telomere-maintenance and cellular-ageing research.
Genomic Stability Research
Telomere dysfunction can contribute to chromosomal instability and altered cellular behaviour.

Epithalon is therefore studied in experimental models examining relationships between telomere integrity, chromosome protection, and genomic stability. Pasted text

This remains a mechanistic research area rather than an established clinical benefit.
Cellular Senescence
Cellular senescence occurs when cells enter a persistent state of growth arrest and undergo changes in gene expression and signalling.

Because telomere shortening can contribute to senescence, researchers have explored whether telomerase-related mechanisms influenced by Epithalon may affect the timing or characteristics of cellular ageing. Pasted text
Pineal and Circadian Research
Epithalon originated from research involving epithalamin and pineal-gland biology.

The pineal gland participates in circadian regulation and melatonin secretion, creating a second major area of Epithalon research beyond telomere biology.

Experimental work has investigated potential effects on:

 	melatonin rhythms;
 	sleep-related endocrine timing;
 	pineal activity;
 	circadian synchronization. Pasted text

Evidence does not establish Epithalon as an approved treatment for insomnia or circadian-rhythm disorders.
Oxidative-Stress Research
Oxidative stress can contribute to cellular injury and may accelerate telomere attrition.

Laboratory research involving Epithalon has therefore examined markers of oxidative stress alongside telomere and ageing-related pathways. Pasted text

The supplied material reports changes in lipid-peroxidation markers and antioxidant-related activity in experimental models.
Replicative Lifespan Research
Cellular experiments have investigated whether alterations in telomerase activity can influence the number of times certain cells can divide before entering replicative senescence.

This has led to Epithalon being discussed in cellular lifespan and longevity research. Pasted text

Cellular lifespan should not be confused with organism or human lifespan.

Ageing involves multiple interacting biological processes rather than one isolated pathway.

The supplied research positions Epithalon at the intersection of:

Product Description
GHK-Cu (Glycyl-L-Histidyl-L-Lysine Copper Complex) is a naturally occurring copper-binding tripeptide studied for its role in tissue repair, extracellular-matrix regulation, wound healing, skin biology, and cellular signalling.

The peptide binds copper ions and has been investigated for its influence on collagen and elastin production, fibroblast activity, angiogenesis, antioxidant defence, inflammatory signalling, and tissue remodelling. Pasted text

GHK-Cu is also of interest in research examining gene-expression patterns associated with repair, metabolism, immune signalling, fibrosis, skin ageing, and cellular regeneration.

The Atlas Longevity GHK-Cu pen contains 100 mg in a 3 mL pre-mixed cartridge with 300 total units/clicks.

GHK-Cu should not be presented as an approved injectable treatment for skin ageing, wound healing, hair loss, fibrosis, or other medical conditions.



Clinical / Research Status
GHK-Cu has been investigated across human, animal, and in-vitro research, including dermatological, cosmetic, wound-healing, fibroblast, and regenerative models.

The supplied material includes research involving:

 	human dermal fibroblasts;
 	human skin and gene-expression profiling;
 	animal wound-healing models;
 	hair-follicle cell cultures;
 	UV-damaged skin models;
 	antioxidant assays;
 	topical and subcutaneous research;
 	extracellular-matrix and tissue-remodelling studies. Pasted text

Evidence strength varies significantly depending on the formulation, route of exposure, study model, and outcome being measured.



Mechanism of Action
GHK-Cu is formed when the GHK tripeptide binds a copper ion.

Copper participates in numerous enzymes involved in tissue repair, antioxidant defence, extracellular-matrix turnover, and normal cellular function.

Experimental research described in the supplied material suggests GHK-Cu may influence:

 	collagen I and III expression;
 	elastin-related pathways;
 	fibroblast activity;
 	metalloproteinases involved in matrix turnover;
 	antioxidant enzymes such as superoxide dismutase;
 	inflammatory pathways including NF-κB;
 	angiogenesis;
 	wound contraction and epithelial repair. Pasted text

The source also describes broad gene-expression effects, although claims involving thousands of genes should be interpreted as transcriptomic research rather than proof of thousands of distinct clinical benefits.

Collagen and Extracellular-Matrix Research
GHK-Cu is widely investigated for its effects on fibroblasts and extracellular-matrix proteins.

Experimental models have reported increased production of collagen and elastin, making the peptide relevant to research examining skin structure, connective tissue, wound healing, and matrix remodelling. Pasted text

These pathways are particularly relevant to regenerative and wound-healing research.

data.description:
MOTS-c 10 mg Pen
Product Description
MOTS-c (Mitochondrial Open Reading Frame of the 12S rRNA type-c) is a 16-amino-acid peptide encoded within mitochondrial DNA and studied for its role in cellular energy regulation, glucose metabolism, lipid metabolism, mitochondrial signalling, and metabolic stress responses.

Unlike most peptides encoded by nuclear DNA, MOTS-c originates from a mitochondrial open reading frame. Research has focused on its ability to act as a metabolic signalling molecule, particularly through pathways associated with AMP-activated protein kinase (AMPK) and cellular responses to energetic stress. Pasted text

Experimental research has examined MOTS-c in relation to:

 	glucose utilisation;
 	insulin signalling;
 	mitochondrial function;
 	fatty-acid metabolism;
 	exercise physiology;
 	oxidative stress;
 	age-associated metabolic changes.

The Atlas Longevity MOTS-c pen contains 10 mg in a 3 mL pre-mixed cartridge with 300 total units/clicks.

MOTS-c remains under preclinical and early human investigation and should not be presented as an approved treatment for diabetes, obesity, metabolic syndrome, ageing, fatigue, or other medical conditions.



Clinical / Research Status
The supplied material describes MOTS-c as remaining in preclinical and early human investigation, despite research spanning several experimental models. Pasted text






Evidence Type
Status Based on Supplied Material




Human clinical research
Early / limited


Human observational research
Yes


Animal research
Yes


In-vitro research
Yes


Regulatory therapeutic approval
Not established






The source labels some evidence as human RCT-level research, but the supporting references provided are dominated by animal studies and reviews.

For Atlas content, the safer characterization is therefore early human plus substantial preclinical research rather than established clinical efficacy.



Evidence Type
The supplied research material includes:

 	observational research in older adults;
 	diet-induced obesity animal models;
 	exercise physiology research;
 	cellular oxidative-stress models;
 	high-fat-diet mouse studies;
 	cultured myocyte research;
 	an early human pilot study referenced by the source;
 	aged-animal longevity research. Pasted text

Results from animal or cellular research should not automatically be treated as established human metabolic outcomes.



Mechanism of Action
MOTS-c is studied as a mitochondrial-derived metabolic signalling peptide.

Under metabolic stress, the supplied material describes MOTS-c as interacting with both mitochondrial and nuclear signalling pathways.

Research mechanisms include:

 	activation of AMPK;
 	interaction with SIRT1;
 	increased PGC-1α-related activity;
 	regulation of GLUT4-associated glucose transport;
 	modulation of fatty-acid metabolism;
 	influence on mitochondrial biogenesis;
 	changes in oxidative-stress pathways;
 	AKT-associated insulin signalling;
 	interaction with mTORC1-related energy balance. Pasted text

The source also describes movement of MOTS-c into the nucleus during metabolic stress, where it may influence gene-expression responses associated with cellular adaptation.

These findings provide a mechanistic basis for research into metabolism and mitochondrial biology but do not establish therapeutic effectiveness.



Potential Benefits / Research Areas
AMPK and Cellular Energy Research
One of the central areas of MOTS-c research involves AMPK, an important cellular energy-sensing pathway.

AMPK responds to changes in cellular energy availability and influences:

 	glucose uptake;
 	fatty-acid oxidation;
 	mitochondrial metabolism;
 	energy conservation;
 	cellular adaptation to stress. Pasted text

MOTS-c is therefore particularly relevant to metabolic-regulation research.
Insulin Signalling and Glucose Utilisation
Experimental studies have investigated whether MOTS-c can influence:

 	insulin sensitivity;
 	glucose tolerance;
 	GLUT4-related glucose transport;
 	cellular glucose uptake.

The supplied material reports changes in these pathways in both preclinical and limited human research contexts. Pasted text

This does not establish MOTS-c as an approved treatment for insulin resistance or diabetes.
Lipid Metabolism Research
MOTS-c has also been studied in animal models examining lipid utilisation.

The supplied material describes increased fatty-acid oxidation and reduced fat accumulation in certain high-fat-diet models. Pasted text

Animal body-composition findings should not be translated into guaranteed human fat-loss outcomes.
Mitochondrial Function
Mitochondrial biology is a major focus of MOTS-c research.

Experimental studies investigate:

 	mitochondrial respiration;
 	ATP-associated energy metabolism;
 	mitochondrial biogenesis;
 	oxidative stress;
 	cellular stress tolerance. Pasted text

Descriptions such as "enhanced mitochondrial efficiency" should be treated as mechanistic research rather than guaranteed clinical benefit.
Metabolic Stress and Ageing Research
MOTS-c has been studied in aged-animal models and other systems involving metabolic stress.

Research areas include:

 	age-associated metabolic decline;
 	high-fat-diet stress;
 	fasting responses;
 	mitochondrial resilience;
 	metabolic homeostasis. Pasted text

These findings make MOTS-c relevant to ageing research, but they do not establish that supplementation slows or reverses human ageing.
Exercise Physiology Research
Experimental MOTS-c studies have also examined:

 	exercise capacity;
 	skeletal-muscle metabolism;
 	substrate utilisation;
 	mitochondrial gene expression;
 	endurance-related markers. Pasted text

Preclinical exercise findings should not be presented as proof of enhanced human athletic performance.
Oxidative-Stress Research
The supplied material describes effects involving stress-response pathways such as:

 	NRF2;
 	FOXO3a;
 	reactive oxygen species;
 	mitochondrial oxidative stress;
 	DNA-protection mechanisms. Pasted text

These pathways are relevant to cellular stress biology but should not be framed as established disease-prevention effects.
Inflammatory-Signalling Research
MOTS-c has also been studied in models involving inflammatory mediators.

The source reports changes involving:

 	IL-6;
 	TNF-α;
 	CRP-related inflammatory pathways. Pasted text

This does not establish MOTS-c as an approved anti-inflammatory treatment.
Neurological and Brain-Energy Research
Emerging research described in the source examines whether mitochondrial peptide signalling may influence neuronal resilience and energy metabolism.

This includes experimental investigation of oxidative stress and mitochondrial function in neural tissue. Pasted text

Claims involving cognitive enhancement or prevention of neurodegenerative disease are not established by the supplied evidence.
Longevity Research
MOTS-c is of particular interest in ageing biology because endogenous mitochondrial signalling changes with age.

The source discusses experimental findings involving:

 	age-related metabolic changes;
 	mitochondrial function;
 	insulin sensitivity;
 	physical performance;
 	lifespan-related animal studies. Pasted text

Animal lifespan findings should not be represented as evidence that MOTS-c extends human lifespan.



Research Data






Study / Model
Reported Finding

Lower endogenous MOTS-c associated with insulin resistance and ageing-related measures

Reduced fat accumulation with improved insulin sensitivity and glucose tolerance

Increased AMPK activity and reduced mitochondrial ROS

Reduced hepatic lipid accumulation and improved metabolic markers

Increased GLUT4 expression and glucose uptake

Subcutaneous exposure described as tolerated, with reported changes in fasting glucose and perceived energy


Aged-mouse studies
Changes in lifespan-related measurements and skeletal-muscle mitochondrial function






The evidence spans very different study designs, and the stronger efficacy claims remain predominantly preclinical. Pasted text



Potential Stack / Combination Research
The supplied source discusses experimental combinations involving MOTS-c with:

 	NAD+;
 	SS-31;
 	BPC-157;
 	Epitalon. Pasted text

The proposed research rationale involves mitochondrial signalling, redox biology, tissue recovery, and ageing-related pathways.

However, the supplied material does not establish validated human safety, efficacy, compatibility, or dosing for these combinations.

They should therefore be treated as experimental research concepts rather than recommended stacks.

Possible Side Effects
The supplied source describes several effects reported or proposed in experimental MOTS-c research.

These include:

 	localized redness or swelling;

The source describes many effects as transient, but human safety evidence remains limited.

Important areas of uncertainty include:

 	glucose-related metabolic effects;
 	endocrine interactions;
 	medication interactions;
 	cardiovascular effects;
 	pregnancy and reproductive exposure;

Because MOTS-c directly influences metabolic signalling pathways, absence of adverse findings in small or early studies should not be interpreted as proof of long-term safety.

Frequently Asked Questions
What is MOTS-c?
MOTS-c is a 16-amino-acid mitochondria-derived peptide encoded within mitochondrial DNA.

It is studied primarily for its role in cellular-energy sensing, metabolic regulation, glucose utilisation, and mitochondrial stress responses. Pasted text
What does MOTS-c stand for?
MOTS-c stands for:

Mitochondrial Open Reading Frame of the 12S rRNA type-c.
Why is MOTS-c different from many other peptides?
Most peptide-coding genes are located within nuclear DNA.

MOTS-c is unusual because it originates from a mitochondrial genomic region, making it part of a growing class of mitochondrial-derived peptides.
How does MOTS-c work?
MOTS-c is studied for its influence on metabolic signalling pathways including:

 	AMPK;
 	SIRT1;
 	PGC-1α;
 	GLUT4-related glucose transport;
 	mitochondrial biogenesis;
 	AKT-related insulin signalling;
 	oxidative-stress pathways. Pasted text

What is AMPK?
AMPK is an important cellular-energy sensor.

When cellular energy availability becomes limited, AMPK can shift metabolism toward pathways that help generate or conserve energy.

MOTS-c research frequently focuses on this pathway.
What is MOTS-c researched for?
Research areas include:

 	mitochondrial function;
 	glucose metabolism;
 	insulin signalling;
 	metabolic stress;
 	lipid metabolism;
 	exercise physiology;
 	oxidative stress;
 	ageing biology;
 	cellular-energy regulation.

Most efficacy evidence remains preclinical.
Has MOTS-c been studied in humans?
Yes, according to the supplied material, there is observational and early human research.

However, MOTS-c remains under early human investigation rather than established clinical use. Pasted text
Does MOTS-c improve insulin sensitivity?
Animal and cellular studies described in the supplied source report changes in insulin sensitivity, GLUT4 expression, glucose uptake, and glucose tolerance. Pasted text

These findings do not establish MOTS-c as an approved treatment for insulin resistance or diabetes.
Does MOTS-c increase endurance?
Experimental studies described by the source report changes in exercise capacity and skeletal-muscle mitochondrial signalling.

However, this does not establish MOTS-c as an approved performance-enhancing treatment.
Does MOTS-c promote fat loss?
Animal models have reported changes in fat accumulation and lipid metabolism.

These preclinical findings should not be interpreted as guaranteed human fat-loss effects.
Does MOTS-c extend lifespan?
The supplied source references aged-mouse research reporting changes in median lifespan and mitochondrial function. Pasted text

Animal lifespan research does not establish that MOTS-c extends human lifespan.

Each Atlas Longevity MOTS-c pen contains:

10 mg in 3 mL.
What is the concentration of the MOTS-c pen?
The concentration is:

10 mg ÷ 3 mL = approximately 3.333 mg/mL
How many clicks are in the pen?

300 total clicks / units

with:

1 click = 0.01 mL
How much MOTS-c is in one click?
Each click contains approximately:

0.0333 mg

or:

33.3 mcg MOTS-c
How many clicks equal 0.5 mg?
15 clicks = 0.50 mg.
How many clicks equal 1 mg?
30 clicks = 1 mg.
How many clicks equal 2 mg?
60 clicks = 2 mg.

These are concentration calculations rather than dosing recommendations.
Can 5 mg be selected in one dial operation?
No.

Mathematically:

5 mg ÷ 0.033333 mg per click ≈150 clicks

The Atlas pen allows a maximum single dial selection of:

60 clicks

Therefore, 5 mg cannot be selected as one dial amount.

This is simply a mechanical and mathematical explanation and does not provide instructions for administering that quantity.

The maximum single dial selection is:

60 clicks

which equals:

0.60 mL

and:

2 mg MOTS-c

This describes the mechanical pen range rather than a recommended amount.
How long does a MOTS-c pen last?
The full cartridge contains:

300 clicks and 10 mg MOTS-c.

The number of administrations depends on the number of clicks selected each time.

For cartridge-capacity calculations only:

 	10 clicks at a time = 30 administrations
 	15 clicks at a time = 20 administrations
 	20 clicks at a time = 15 administrations
 	30 clicks at a time = 10 administrations
 	60 clicks at a time = 5 administrations

These examples describe cartridge capacity only.
Does the medication disappear when the dial returns to zero?
No.

After administration, the dial returns to zero while the unused formulation remains inside the cartridge.

The remaining MOTS-c stays in the pen until all 300 units have been used.

@graph.name: Are Ozempic and Wegovy the same drug?

@graph.name: What is the difference between a GLP-1 drug and a GLP-1/GIP drug?

acceptedAnswer.text: A GLP-1 drug, such as semaglutide, activates one incretin receptor. A GLP-1/GIP drug, such as tirzepatide, activates two. Both lower blood sugar and reduce appetite.

@graph.name: Can I switch from Ozempic to Mounjaro?

@graph.name: How long do retatrutide side effects last?

The full TRIUMPH-1 results reported symptoms of low blood pressure. They were dose-dependent and more common in people who were also taking blood pressure medicines.

@graph.name: Can I Take Semaglutide if My Mother Had Thyroid Cancer?

acceptedAnswer.text: It depends on the type. A family history of medullary thyroid carcinoma rules out both semaglutide and tirzepatide. Other thyroid cancers are not on the contraindication list, but tell your doctor about any family history.

@graph.name: Can I Take Tirzepatide With Birth Control Pills?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, but with a backup. The Mounjaro label advises switching to a non-oral method, or adding a barrier method, for four weeks after starting and after each dose increase.

@graph.name: Is Semaglutide Safe if I Have Had Pancreatitis?

acceptedAnswer.text: Not automatically. Pancreatitis is a label warning for both drugs, so your doctor will weigh your history before deciding.

@graph.name: Can I Take Semaglutide While Breastfeeding?

acceptedAnswer.text: There is not enough data to say. The label asks you and your doctor to weigh the benefits of breastfeeding against your need for the medicine.

@graph.name: Can I Use Semaglutide and Tirzepatide Together?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. The Wegovy label does not recommend combining semaglutide with any other GLP-1 receptor agonist, and tirzepatide acts on the GLP-1 receptor too.

@graph.name: Do I Need to Stop These Drugs Before Surgery?

acceptedAnswer.text: Tell your surgeon or anaesthetist that you take them. Both labels warn about a rare risk of inhaling stomach contents under anaesthesia, and your care team will decide what to do.

acceptedAnswer.text: Mostly stomach and gut effects, such as nausea, constipation and vomiting. In REDEFINE 1, most were mild to moderate, and 5.9% of people stopped treatment because of side effects.

itemListElement.name: Survodutide and Eloralintide: Who Makes Them, and Are They Approved?

acceptedAnswer.text: Eloralintide is an investigational once-weekly injection from Eli Lilly that copies the hormone amylin. It is a selective amylin receptor agonist being tested for weight management, and it is not approved yet.
Survodutide is an investigational once-weekly injection that acts on the glucagon and GLP-1 receptors. Boehringer Ingelheim develops it under licence from Zealand Pharma, and it is not approved yet.

@graph.name: Is Survodutide Approved by the FDA?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. Survodutide has finished its main phase 3 obesity trials, and Boehringer says it is preparing regulatory submissions, but no filing or decision date has been announced.
No date has been announced. Its phase 3 trials began at the end of 2025, so results, a filing and a regulatory review all still lie ahead.

@graph.name: Is Eloralintide the Same as Cagrilintide?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. Both copy amylin, but they are different molecules from different companies. Cagrilintide is from Novo Nordisk and is combined with semaglutide in CagriSema, while eloralintide is Lilly's own amylin drug.

There is no head-to-head trial to say. Survodutide reached up to 16.6% weight loss in its phase 3 trial without diabetes, but trials of different drugs used different people and lengths, so the figures cannot be compared directly.
